summary:
OrBEATs is a web experience that helps people explore our changing planet through sound. Developed for the Earth Information Jukebox challenge, it brings NASA visualizations and scientific explanations together with musical interpretations, interactive sound, and NASA-narrated journeys.

In Explore, visitors can hear interpretations of forest heights, changing carbon dioxide patterns, and disappearing Arctic ice. Interactive experiences generate sounds as users explore ocean and aerosol visualizations, connecting what they hear to the features they select. Each journey explains its scientific source and what its sounds represent, distinguishing illustrative music from data-based mappings. A rhythm game extends discovery through play, while the Compose experience lets users experiment with environmental variables and musical responses, save their music, like other people's music, and choose the OrBEAT of the week. 

We designed OrBEATs with blind and low-vision learners in mind, incorporating keyboard controls, audio guidance, and adjustable visual settings. Our goal is to give families, students, and museum visitors more ways to explore Earth science together, making changes in our planet easier to notice, discuss, and understand.
details:
OrBEATs is an interactive Earth science website developed for NASA Space Apps’ “The Earth Information Jukebox” challenge. It transforms NASA visualizations into experiences that users can both see and hear, helping students, the general public, and blind and low-vision users explore environmental patterns through sound. By pairing visual information with meaningful audio, OrBEATs aims to make complex Earth science more approachable, engaging, and accessible.

The website brings together experiences covering ocean temperatures and currents, aerosols, air quality, atmospheric carbon dioxide, forest heights, night lights, and lightning. Each experience uses a sound mapping suited to the phenomenon being presented. Ocean temperature estimates influence musical pitch, aerosol types have distinct tones, visible lightning events trigger notes, and carbon dioxide pulses drive a heartbeat-like rhythm. Forest-height colors create a changing melody, while night-light patterns influence musical intensity and texture. These mappings help users connect what they hear with specific features in NASA’s visualizations.

OrBEATs combines interactive exploration with automatically sonified videos. Users can select an ocean region and follow its changing sound and temperature trace, or move their cursor across an aerosol image to hear the categories represented beneath it. Other experiences use highlighted listening windows or fixed scan lines to show which part of a visualization is generating the sound. This makes the relationship between the imagery and audio visible and easier to follow.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the website, browser audio capabilities for interactive sound generation, and Python for processing visual information and producing sonified audio and video. AI tools supported audio generation and sonification development, guided by our team’s interpretation of the visualizations and the scientific information provided by NASA. We designed the mappings to communicate environmental features rather than simply add background music.

Accessibility was a central design consideration. OrBEATs includes keyboard controls, screen-reader labels, audio explanations, captions, and volume controls, providing multiple ways to navigate and understand the experiences. We also considered sound clarity, synchronization, visual guidance, and consistency within each experience.

Scientific transparency informed our approach. Where sound is generated from rendered colors or image changes, it represents an interpretation of those visual features rather than an exact physical measurement. We distinguish these estimates from underlying scientific data and avoid presenting musical intensity as a validated danger level.

Our team and mentors tested the website’s functionality and experiences during development. OrBEATs’ intended impact is to broaden participation in Earth science by offering complementary ways to explore it: users can observe a pattern, hear its changes, and actively investigate the connection.
